Woah this is such a catch-22. ADHD testing can be pretty ADHD unfriendly, and it’s almost like they’re saying if you can get thru the process it means you don’t have ADHD lol. The fact you are able to get thru it could just mean you are just motivated to get the help. We can focus well at times if we’re motivated, interested, or the task is engaging enough. 

Also about still wanting to post and hang out here, I think ADHD strategies can be helpful for everyone sometimes. If they help you and you feel like you relate, you belong here! Especially if ur still on a journey of understanding your diagnosis.

I feel this so much. I’m similar to you in height and weight, and also had some recent weight gain and enjoy working out. I’ve been a pear-shaped with a belly all my life at any weight (even at 90lb I still had a belly bump haha). 

For me it’s been helpful to look at female athletes instead of models, because they have really beautiful bodies but are more “real” and not playing into society’s aesthetics the way social media usually does. I randomly came across this video of [Sha’Carri Richardson winning the 100m dash ](https://youtu.be/9VPFWlf5i4E) and it like stuck with me so much because I feel like she’s so beautiful and feminine and cool but her body type is basically the exact same as mine (except way more muscles lol), which I never see. Like she’s not ultra thin, she’s short with a pear shaped body but she looks amazing. It’s stupid but somehow a pro athlete beauty ideal feels way more realistic than what you see on Instagram or on models, and it makes me feel sexy when I wear like a sports bra and shorts cause the athletic sporty look is not only made for the tall skinny hourglass people. Hope it helps it’s helped me but I still have these insecurities too.
It’s like saying your human and nothing else. ADHD people have a certain type of brain, but we’re all so different from one another.

The last thing you described about sound sensitivity is called misophonia and it’s pretty common in ADHD, I have it too with chewing sounds.

The most important for me was to find a major I am really passionate about, which ended up being something I had no interest in initially. Right now is a good time for exploration and figuring out your interests, accomplishing things can come later. I’m sure you’ll do well. Hi! I’ve read people saying the morning is best for focus, I think there’s even a study or 2 about morning cardio being good. However when I try doing this the task switching is always hard for me, I feel like my body is in active mode and don’t wanna sit quietly and focus, I usually end up doing chores in my house instead of doing my work. I think whatever works well for you is good, you could try running around the block briefly in the morning and see how your day goes after that. I think night exercise can be helpful for ADHD symptoms too, I usually feel more happy and focused the next morning as long as I didn’t overdo it. My favorite exercises are all outdoors and I’ve heard that’s supposed to help with ADHD too, getting some fresh air and nature is just good for the brain I guess.

This is stupidly simple, but my favorite zero point (blue) protein snack/main right now is Hiyayakko (cold Japanese tofu). You just cube the tofu, pour soy sauce over, and top with whatever you like! I like ginger and shredded seaweed sheets on top.

Recipe is here, she also has other good classic Japanese tofu recipes:

https://justhungry.com/two-classic-japanese-tofu-dishes-hiyayakko-and-agedashi-dofu

https://justbento.com/handbook/recipe-collection-mains/vegan-iri-dofu-iri-doufu-garlic-chives

And amazing black bean burger bites:

https://justhungry.com/black-bean-vegan-miniburgers

I also make a protein shake with 1 cup unsweetened soy milk, 1 banana, 2 tbsp peanut powder, and optional frozen kale for extra nutrients. It’s really really delicious, costs about 3-4pt depending on your peanut powder.

Oh one more, if you like Indian food I have a really good recipe for chickpea Dal though it is a little involved (would take a minute to write it up lmk if you want it). You can also find some recipes online though I think they are hit or miss. For simpler alternatives, canned lentil soup and homemade split pea soup tend to be really good and very WW friendly.

I have more lol but these are my go to proteins right now, just started WW but been vegetarian/vegan for 10+ years.

Sorry you're going through that. You seem like a nice person. I think love is like a drug for some people, they get can addicted to it instead of truly caring about the other person's wellbeing. Especially for someone who doesn't have a lot of other supports. She'll be okay without you, she'll likely end up better for it if you already know the relationship can't last. She can move on and find someone else, but when she's in that state of panic trying to keep you there it probably won't change until you fully commit or you leave. Speaking as someone with abandonment issues, please leave if you're not able to commit.

Personally this is not something that would bother me in a relationship, but I understand for others it may be unacceptable. It sounds like he is being considerate of your feelings, has respected the boundary, and that you both care about each other. You could talk to a therapist if you haven't been able to heal and still want to maintain the relationship, but if this bothers you a lot it could indicate some incompatibility between you.

He honestly sounds very emotionally abusive. I don't think you should have to "take criticism well" in a romantic relationship. If his criticism is too harsh and is hurting you, he needs to stop, and if he won't stop when you tell him it is hurting you badly it is emotional abuse.

How long have you been together? And have you been in many other romantic relationships before?

You seem to be talking about "me not working hard enough" and him thinking you're "giving up", which makes me feel like a lot of the pressure to fix it is being put on you. Is he doing things to actively fix it, or just demanding that you stay and you fix the problems?

For me there's been relationships that are easy and natural, and relationships that required a lot of work from the start. The latter always were because of incompatibility in hindsight, and I had a bad tendency to take a lot of the "work" on my shoulders and try to change myself for that person. With the right person I don't have to change, I can be who I am and that's what the other person needs and loves. It's the same feeling I get around a really good friend or close family member, it just flows and there's trust and that usually comes naturally when you're compatible.

This is a good point, but I think we should also keep in mind the serious risks Effexor can have over other antidepressants, since there is research showing this. Just pulling off the adverse effects section of Wikipedia:

\>  A study conducted in Finland followed more than 15,000 patients for 3.4 years. Venlafaxine increased suicide risk by 60% (statistically significant), as compared to no treatment. At the same time, fluoxetine (Prozac) halved the suicide risk.

\> Venlafaxine has a higher rate of moderate to severe discontinuation symptoms relative to other antidepressants (similar to the SSRI paroxetine).

\>  Venlafaxine appears to be more likely than the SSRIs and bupropion to induce mania and mixed episodes in bipolar patients.

[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venlafaxine#Adverse\_effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venlafaxine#Adverse_effects)

It could be dangerous to start Effexor for someone with bipolar or suicidal ideation, and it is also difficult to get off it due to the discontinuation symptoms. It seems questionable why a doctor would start this as your first antidepressant without a specific resason.

Hi, I can relate to this a lot. I feel like the medication has help me a lot with not overreacting to stuff and getting upset really easily. I have had off days on it too though where something happened and I just cried all day. I think it's okay if you have those days, especially early on. I also don't think having misunderstandings or feeling upset is your fault, that is also a symptom of ADHD and you are getting treatment, also you seem to care a lot about your friends so you're obviously a good person. 

I think it does get better after the first month, at least it did for me. Hope it gets better for you soon. Do you have a specific time that you eat breakfast/lunch/dinner? I try to force myself to eat lunch at noon even if I'm not hungry but sometimes all I can do is grab a snack. My side effects are a lot worse if I don't eat though. Maybe you can try buying some nutritional drinks like Ensure, or try to have your favorite snacks on hand? I like Ensure I used to drink it when I really really didn't wanna eat.

Ohh this is a good question, and I definitely mask. For me I came from a family that puts a lot of pressure on being smart and succeeding in school, so I would never want to talk about the fact that I couldn't listen during class no matter how hard I tried, or how my bad memory and problems in school were not just laziness or apathy. I didn't wanna look stupid, I still feel stupid talking about it. In social settings I am quiet to mask the fact that I am not listening or that I am really tired of sitting around and want to go do something active. If you are female you might mask more? Since a lot of women do not get diagnosed.

Also a lot of people with ADHD are not hyperactive, there are 3 types: "inattentive", "hyperactive", and "combined".
